Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

tflspec (development version)

  • AI requests: the shell sheet first, the TOC as candidates (0.0.24.9234). A request is a shell sheet’s (unit = "sheet", the default of tfl_ai_prepare() / tfl_ai_write_requests()): what the sheet writes comes first – its numbers, titles, populations, conditions, layout and variables – then its sheet name, then its TOC candidates, each with the clues that chose it (a number written in the sheet, the sheet name’s number, a close number, the title’s words); the TOC and the sheet names can hold mistakes, and the AI says which it chose and why. The reports and their ids are the AI’s to read from the sheet (a TOC item made by two Part sheets, a sheet of several reports); collecting does not hold them to a list – an id no TOC item has is a warning, and a sheet that is no shell is answered with no report. Every TOC sheet is read (Topline_TOC too), an item once with the TOC sheets listing it (toc_sheets); the TOC items no sheet chose are asked for in one request (no-shell). sheet_roles = c("Topline TOC" = "other") changes a sheet’s role. No part is guessed any more (a heading’s format sample “Table 15.1.2.x” was read as parts): parts, parts_row and part_of go. A dry run’s toc is a TOC item a row (toc_id, toc_sheets, sheets, request), shells a shell sheet a row (candidates, guessed, request) and counts the numbers of each. unit = "toc": the requests as before. The workbook is read about three times as fast (a sheet’s cells at once), and a TOC’s header of two rows (Title merged over its parts) says its titles.

  • A TOC’s columns by their role (0.0.24.9234): the item’s number and its shell’s apart, the title(s), the population, the program and file names from the headers’ words (Output No, Shell, Title, Population, Program, File, and the Japanese words), or toc_cols = c(output_id = "Output No", shell = "Shell", title = c("Title 1", "Title 2")) (a header or a column’s letter); the row’s other columns go to its requests as “header: value”.

  • In a table with columns (table_plan(cols = TRT01A)), every analysis has its by (0.0.24.9233): one without is a problem of the study’s ARD definition that says the by to write (by: [TRT01A]), but for the columns’ own count (the N), a custom analysis, one inside another and the study’s N; by: [] (in the sheet (none)) says an analysis has no columns. A by the data does not have stops the program, as before.

  • Named sets of records (0.0.24.9231): sheet records (record_id, dataset, where, label, any_label), data.yml records: (- {id: TESAE, dataset: ADAE, where: !r ..., label: ..., any_label: Any SAE}); an analysis’s records: TESAE reads the set’s dataset under its condition, its own where on top, and the program’s data of it is commented with the set. A hierarchy of a set with its “any” row (over_variables = TRUE) is labelled with the set’s any_label, else Any <id>, when the table’s normalize_ard() (or its overall_label) says none.

  • The data the ARD program makes itself is named <dataset>_sub (0.0.24.9229): an analysis set’s (adsl_sub, was pop_saf) and an analysis’s own records (adae_sub, was adae_saf), numbered from a report’s second of a dataset (adsl_sub2), each under a comment saying what it is (# adsl_sub: SAF — Safety Analysis Set (SAFFL == "Y")). In the study’s program each report’s part makes its own, so a name means one thing in a report. R in the definition (code, args, where) writes the new names; an old pop_<id> there is a problem that says the new one. The names of analysis data a person gives (data_id) do not change. tfl_ard_data_names() says each analysis’s data by the program’s name.

  • An agent’s requests and AGENTS.md always say where the TOC / SHELL workbook and the ADaM are, from the study folder, and that the agent may open them to check what a request leaves unclear – above all a shell’s shape (several parts, a part that writes only what differs, merged cells); when it cannot open them (outside its workspace, no permission), it decides from the request alone (0.0.24.9228). What an agent may read is the workspace’s to say, not the request’s.

  • Named values in the ARD definition (0.0.24.9227): sheet objects (output_id, object_id, code, label), data.yml objects: for the study’s and a report’s ard: objects: for its own, each {id, code: !r ..., label}. The ARD program makes them at its top (id <- code, the label a comment above), the study’s before a report’s; an analysis names one as its denominator, or in its args or where. Checked: an R name, not a dataset’s or pop_*, once in its scope, code that is R.

  • Table sheets keep what they cannot say (#448): YAML -> sheets -> YAML no longer drops a table’s items the sheets cannot hold (plan_titles, plan_after, a second call of a verb, a plan_digits() with stat, a plan_style() border with more than its sides, plan_columns() widths by position …): an item any of whose arguments no column says goes whole, as YAML, into the tables sheet’s new column content_more (not into the other sheets as well), and is read back into the content by its verb’s rank. The defaults’ items too. A table’s (or a listing’s) verb called twice is put together in one call when the content is read, as rtfreporter puts the two layers together – a later call’s arguments winning, key by key; plan_hide()’s columns adding up – and a message says so; the verbs whose calls are layers of their own (filters, comparisons, cell styles, steps after, titles of other pages) are left as they are, and a figure’s content is not touched (0.0.24.9226).

  • Listing sheets keep what their columns cannot say (#447): YAML -> sheets -> YAML no longer drops a listing’s other items (plan_hide, plan_paginate_group, a plan_paginate_rows() with page_by, …) or a column’s other listing_col() arguments (name, rel_width, layout): the listings sheet’s new column content_more holds those items as YAML, the listing_cols sheet’s more a column’s other arguments, and they are read back as they were (0.0.24.9226).

  • An analysis’s denominator can be numbers (0.0.24.9225): one (denominator: 86, every column’s N) or one a value of the analysis’s by (denominator: {Drug X: 86, Placebo: 85}, in the sheet c("Drug X" = 86, "Placebo" = 85)). The ARD program writes the one as 86L and the other as that many subjects of each arm (data.frame(TRT01A = rep(...), USUBJID = seq_len(...))), which cards counts the same way for a tabulation and a nested count. A vector without names, a number not whole, or by of more than one variable is a problem of the definition.

  • Fonts per script and their languages (#449, rtfreporter#715): a font table entry’s name is one family or a family per script slot (latin, east_asian, complex, hansi), the titles’ and footnotes’ font too; page.rtf_document.font_lang gives a slot’s language (east_asian: ja). The report’s rtf_document() call writes them as rtfreporter takes them (named vectors), the study setup as options(rtfreporter.font =, rtfreporter.font_lang =), and the page sheet’s font / new font_lang columns say them as latin = X | east_asian = Y – before, a slotted family was lost on the sheets’ path. rtfreporter (>= 0.8.2.9094) (0.0.24.9223).

  • The running header’s and footer’s look (#450): page.rtf_header and page.rtf_footer take rtfreporter’s rtf_header() / rtf_footer() arguments (border, width, width_twips, row_height_twips, font_size_half_points, font, markup, cell_padding_*, drop_empty_rows; the lines stay page.header / page.footer), and page.rtf_footnotes a border. The report’s call and the study setup’s study_header / study_footer write them; a report whose look differs from the study’s writes its own call.

  • Page sheets keep the page arguments no column says (#451): YAML -> sheets -> YAML no longer drops a page’s other rtfreporter arguments (the titles’ row height, the running header’s look, the figure’s align, a second font …): the page sheet’s new column page_more holds them as YAML and they are read back as they were.

  • rtf_figures()’s drawing, the study’s rtfreporter options, overwrite (#452): page.rtf_figures takes render_width, render_height, render_dpi and png_device (rtfreporter#719; a drawn figure’s rtfplot() gets the device too); defaults.yml’s options: names rtfreporter’s options (rtfreporter.png_device, rtfreporter.figure.default_dpi, rtfreporter.ard_pipe …), which the study setup writes as options(); page.generate_rtfreport.overwrite says whether a report’s file may be written over, read by the new tfl_report_overwrite() (and tfl_ai_run()). rtfreporter (>= 0.8.2.9096).

  • A report’s own data: with a figure template (#446): its steps (the data stage: the analysis set, the parameter, the records kept) come first, then the template’s call steps (the fit and what the call makes from it); the template’s call stays on, and tfl_template_to_spec() writes the same. Before, the report’s steps replaced the template’s whole list, the fit with it. Without own steps, and for a table’s template, nothing changes (0.0.24.9222).

  • No page argument is dropped any more (#444): page.rtf_titles and page.rtf_footnotes write row_height_twips, markup, font and align (not only font_size_half_points), page.rtf_figures its align, and page.rtf_tables a font_size_half_points left on the page (a content of R code) – the schema took them, the program left them out. markup takes rtfreporter’s words ("script", "relational", "all", "none"), no longer TRUE / FALSE (0.0.24.9217).

  • A report on the page of the content before it (#443): a report’s page.rtf_tables says page_break, space_before, first_rows and cont_title, and page.rtf_figures page_break and space_before, as rtfreporter’s rtf_tables() / rtf_figures() take them; the report sheet has the same columns. The generated call passes them only when the report is not on a page of its own (page_break: false). They take effect in a document that holds content before the report’s (0.0.24.9216).

  • tfl_ai_prepare()’s toc (a dry run’s too) says each report’s parts, parts_row and same_number, as tfl_ai_read_shell()$toc does: a caller need not read the workbook again (0.0.24.9213).

  • The AI requests’ defaults (0.0.24.9212): size = NULL holds one report a request with mode = "agent" (each answer checked and built before the next) and, in a chat, 3 (tfl_ai_prepare()) or 8 (tfl_ai_write_requests()) as before; instructions = "once" is the default (a chat’s instructions in 00-instructions.md, its requests without them). With mode = "agent" the instructions are always written once, ai/instructions-table.md / -figure.md, whichever instructions says.

  • A report’s parts, and requests written fast (0.0.24.9211).

    • A report whose shell sheet holds it in parts (Table 15.1.5.1.a above, .b below, the later often only what differs) is found: tfl_ai_read_shell()$toc says parts (the parts’ ids, the TOC’s number with the letter: t.15.1.5.1.a | t.15.1.5.1.b) and parts_row (the row each starts on), and its request asks for a report file a part (the layout the first part’s). Answers with the parts’ ids are the report’s (not reports too many), and spec/toc.yml lists the parts in its place.
    • A number’s part letter after a dot, a dash or an underscore (.a, -a, _a) is the number’s, as one written straight on (T15.1.5.1A); a TOC row of a part with no sheet of its own reads its parent’s sheet whole. A number the TOC names twice warns (same_number; its first row kept).
    • The table instructions (ai/instructions-table.md, a chat’s prompt) always say that a sheet can hold a report’s parts (Part 1 / Part 2, Phase 1 / Phase 2): a report file a part, its id the shell’s number or the TOC’s with .a, .b, the layout the first part’s, the split an assumption. The request adds the parts’ rows when they are found.
    • size = 1: a request is named after its report’s number (ai/requests/t.15.1.5.1.md).
    • A request’s shell is cut from the workbook as it was read, not read again from the file a request at a time: 46 reports’ requests in about 30 seconds, where a workbook of many sheets took half an hour. Each request is written as it is made (index.md at the end), and progress = function(step, i, n) on tfl_ai_prepare() / tfl_ai_write_requests() says where the work is ("adam", "workbook", "request" i of n).

  • The layouts’ parameters: what a report changes (0.0.24.9208). summary (42 parameters, now 15) and hierarchical (33, now 15) keep only what one report’s table differs from another’s in; the look (the stub, blank rows, widths, rounding, the column header) and the page are the study standard’s – change them after the template, tfl_tpl(...) |> plan_stub(...) – and the ARD’s ids and labels are the layout’s own (the template’s label). The layout’s page (summary: 30 rows, group_safe; hierarchical: 22, group_force) gives way to a study standard’s plan_paginate_rows(); hierarchical’s column header (its n (%) line) stays the table’s. Renamed after the parameter naming rules: cat_cell / cell -> count_cell, statistics -> continuous_statistics, cat_statistics -> categorical_statistics, overall -> any_row (TRUE / FALSE) and any_row_label. The study’s tables are as before.

  • stf_t02_demog: demog in the shape of FDA STF IG v2 Table 2 (Sex, Age as Mean (SD) and Median (min, max), age groups, race, ethnicity, country; a Total column). It is not endorsed or recommended by FDA. demog’s label is now “Demographics”.

  • orr(stat_layout = "cols"): each arm’s N over its two columns (0.0.24.9207), as the default layout has it under the arm: rtfreporter (>= 0.8.2.9090) reads it over split columns (ichirio/rtfreporter#709).

  • run.R’s status of a request not run this time (0.0.24.9205): Rscript run.R <request> built that request’s reports alone, and ai/status.md said of another, never built, “the report files are written”, and of one whose last build failed, nothing. A report not built yet now says so, with its Rscript run.R line; a failed build is kept in ai/built.csv and said again. A report that could not be built has no RTF (or PNG) left of an earlier run: they are removed.

  • The figure templates are called as the tables’: tfl_tpl(<data>, "<name>", ...) (0.0.24.9204, #430), and a report’s program calls it: content <- tfl_tpl(adtte_ttdisc, "km_disc", group = TRT01A). The arguments of the data steps (population, param, data, where, event: tfl_param(stage = "data")) are the program’s, not the call’s. The figures’ own functions (tpl_km_simple() …) stay and draw as before.

    • One Kaplan-Meier layout, km, its look as arguments: y_type (survival or risk, 1 - S(t)), y_percent, ci ("band", or "bars": the CI at the axis’s times, geom_errorbar()), censor_marks, median_line, risk_table (risk_title, risk_stats …), pvalue, x_max / x_by, the labels, the legend, event (CNSR made from a condition: ADSL’s EOTSTT == "DISCONTINUED"), time_unit and plot (any other setting). The figure style’s km values a study changes (censor_shape, risk_title …) are the study’s values of their parameters (tfl_param(study = "km.<key>")).
    • km_disc (FDA STF Figure 1: time to permanent discontinuation, the cumulative % in weeks, the CI as bars, the log-rank p-value), km_ae_onset (Figure 4) and km_lfu (Figure 13) are its parameter sets; km_simple, km_risk_table and km_ci too, their designs as before.
    • The generated code of .content_fig_tpl_code() lives in R/tpl_fig_code.R.

  • A template’s help (#429, 0.0.24.9203): tfl_tpl_args(name, study, population) is a template’s parameters as a table – tier, the layout’s default, the default a variant changes, the study standard’s value, the value in effect and its layer ("study", "variant:<name>", "template") – and tfl_tpl_help() prints it by tier. Each table and listing template has its page, ?tfl_tpl_<name> (?tfl_tpl_demog), made from the registry when the documentation is built (roxygen @eval); a test says when one is missing or out of date.

  • tfl_tpl(x, name, ...): one call for every table and listing template (0.0.24.9202), and a report’s program calls it: tfl_tpl(ard, "demog", population = "SAF"). The template’s own functions (tpl_demog() …) and tfl_template_run() stay.

    • The layouts summary and hierarchical take a table’s whole look as parameters (order, total, heading, header_n, rounding, stub_*, blanks*, widths, max_rows, split …), each in a tier (tfl_param(tier = "required" / "usual" / "other")); those whose study names a study standard’s item take its value, and the program’s call says them, with no # (study default) lines after it.
    • demog is summary with its own defaults (summary’s variables is now continuous); ae_soc_pt is hierarchical’s, and ae_ser_soc_pt (serious TEAEs, “Any SAE”) and ae_disc_soc_pt (TEAEs leading to discontinuation) are ae_soc_pt’s. min_pct on hierarchical; stack = TRUE on summary.
    • tfl_templates() says each one’s label and whether the AI kit uses it (ai; tfl_template(ai = ), tfl_template_variant(ai = , example = )).

  • orr(stat_layout = "cols"): each arm’s rate and its CI side by side (0.0.24.9201), on the layout stat_block; the best overall response’s n (%) in the first of the two columns. The arms’ N is not in that header yet (rtfreporter does not read it over split columns, ichirio/rtfreporter#709). The default, "rows", is the table as before.

  • A study copied elsewhere checks its answers against its own files (0.0.24.9200). The requests’ contexts (ai/requests/_contexts.rds) kept the study folder’s path of the PC that wrote them, and an answer’s check read the study’s files there; they now keep none, and tfl_ai_collect_answers() (and run.R) use the folder they are run in – requests written before included.

  • An agent’s requests say an agent’s next steps: ai/requests/index.md and ai/status.md’s next steps name ai/agent_prompt.md, the answer to save and Rscript run.R <request>, not a chat to paste into.

  • A report that could not be built: its repair is a file of its own (0.0.24.9199), ai/repairs/<request>-build.md, which stays until the request’s reports are built: tfl_ai_collect_answers() – run again between, by a screen’s reload – removes only the checks’ repair (<request>.md), and took the build’s with it. ai/status.md and the agent’s instructions name the file.

  • demog and ae_pt_freq are built on their layouts (0.0.24.9198): demog’s usual table is summary’s body (its own code stays for stack = TRUE and a dataset other than ADSL), ae_pt_freq is hierarchical’s of one level with its own order, min_pct filter and page. Their ARDs, items and programs are as before. hierarchical with one level (hierarchy = "AEDECOD") no longer stops: it has no row keys above the term.

  • tfl_ai_run() (run.R) builds only what changed (0.0.24.9197). A report’s ARD and RTF are made again only when its report file, the study’s files (study.yml, spec/data.yml, spec/defaults.yml, its templates), the ADaM it reads or the packages’ versions changed since the last run (ai/built.csv); else its RTF is kept. requests = (Rscript run.R ae-1) builds one request’s reports, every answer still read and checked; rebuild = TRUE builds them all. A report that passed its checks but could not be built gets a repair, ai/repairs/<request>.md, with why. The agent’s instructions and each request name Rscript run.R <request>. In a study of 100 reports a run after one answer goes from minutes to seconds.

  • A study’s AI files name its paths from the study folder (0.0.24.9196). tfl_ai_prepare(mode = "agent")’s first message for the agent (ai/agent_prompt.md, $agent_prompt) names AGENTS.md, ai/requests/index.md, run.R … from the study folder, not with this PC’s path; the requests name a TOC / SHELL workbook in the study folder from it, however it was given (relative, with backslashes, another case); tfl_ai_study_init() writes an ADaM folder in the study, given whole, from it in spec/data.yml. A study copied to another PC then says the same. A workbook or ADaM folder outside the study keeps its whole path.

  • The layout template stat_block: one record’s statistics over several rows and columns (0.0.24.9195). Each arm’s block holds one analysis record’s statistics – its N in one column, its rate and interval in the next, or under each other – as cells says: a named list, heading = template, one element a column (direction = "cols") or a row ("rows"), a vector its lines (cells = list(N = "{N}", "ORR(%) 90%CI" = c("{n} ({estimate:.1f%})", "{conf.low:.1f%}, {conf.high:.1f%}")); in YAML, records {label, template}). The statistics each group shows are read from its templates; the ARD is the report’s own (so, as km_table, it takes no subset or where). tpl_stat_block() is the call. Needs rtfreporter 0.8.2.9086 (a split record takes its group’s template, whatever the study’s categorical).

  • orr: conf_level (0.95): the rate’s CI’s level, and its row’s label (90% CI). The template is now tagged as the stat_block layout; with the defaults it writes the same table as before.

  • The template vs_change and tpl_vs_change() are removed (0.0.24.9194). Its table is param_change with baseline = TRUE and layout = "rows": one parameter (params), one visit (visits), vs_change’s statistics, cells and labels (baseline_label, value_label, change_label) give the same rows and cells. The one difference is param_change’s blocks of the parameter and the visit; a report that wants them in the title removes them with its own plan_* items. A report file with template: {name: vs_change} is now an error naming the templates there are.

  • Templates: the standard filter pair, subset (which subjects) and where (which records) (0.0.24.9193). Every table and figure template takes subset, an R condition on the analysis set’s ADSL – the denominator, the header N and, through the three stages, the records – and every template of records data where. tfl_param() gets group ("target": population, subset, where, listed first); tfl_test_templates() lists a template without them. A listing keeps ADSL’s subjects by a semi join; km_table has no data of its own and takes neither. An analysis set narrowed by a report’s own condition is one statement when the set is used for nothing else (adsl_saf <- filter(adsl, SAFFL == "Y", PART == "Part 1")).

  • param_change: a baseline block (baseline = TRUE, baseline_label; 0.0.24.9193). The baseline’s rows (BASE) come before the value’s. With vs_change’s statistics, cells and labels, param_change gives vs_change’s rows and cells; its blocks of the parameter and the visit are the one difference. vs_change stays for now.

  • Generated ARD programs in three stages: the denominator, the target subjects, the target records (0.0.24.9192). A records dataset is joined to its subjects: inner_join() when it takes ADSL columns (an explicit add, and the by / strata of analyses with a denominator; never record-level columns the population’s derive makes, such as TRTA), the records’ own columns of those names dropped first; semi_join() otherwise. The report’s where is its own filter() after the join, and a dataset as a denominator is a semi_join() too. Analyses on the same dataset, analysis set and where share one object, with the union of the ADSL columns they need. See tfl_ard_code()’s details.

  • Generated code pipes with |> (0.0.24.9192). The report programs’ pipe was RStudio’s Insert Pipe Operator setting, and %>% outside RStudio, while the ARD programs wrote |>; now every program writes |> unless asked (pipe = "%>%" / "rstudio", or the option rtfreporter.ard_pipe).

  • The AI flow with templates: tfl_ai_prepare(templates = TRUE) (0.0.24.9191). The requests ask the AI to answer a report with one of the study’s templates where one fits (template: {name, args}, only the arguments that differ, the report’s own content items after it), else as a code SPEC; the templates are listed from the registry (tflspec’s, a company’s, a study’s variants, the target arguments marked) when the requests are written, never by hand. An answer’s template is checked (its name, its arguments’ names and types) and expanded, so the code SPEC’s checks run on what it stands for; the report file keeps the template, and its RTF or PNG is built as any other. Each request’s first line and ai/status.md say the setting. templates = FALSE asks for the code SPEC only: a chat’s requests are byte for byte as before. tfl_ai_compare() (new) sets the two side by side: one row a report – answered with a template or code, its report file’s values, its check, its repairs – in ai/compare.csv.

    • mode = "agent": what every request repeated is written once in ai/ – instructions-table.md, instructions-figure.md (the instructions and the schema), templates.md – and the ADaM summary and spec/ files are named, not copied; a request names them, its own answer header and the templates likely for each report (from its title). A request drops from about 53,000 to 4,000 characters; with templates = FALSE the agent’s requests take the same form. tfl_ai_write_requests() has a mode argument for this.
    • A chat’s request over max_chars with templates first lists their arguments by name only, then is halved as before.

  • Figure templates: the design form, and tpl_ functions that draw only (#403, 0.0.24.9190). A template SPEC’s figure expands into the design form (data steps, plot, layers), as the figure designer and the AI drafts write it; a report’s own items after template: go onto it (a dashed line, the numbers from an ARD, labs). As for tables, the program writes the data steps (the analysis set’s semi join, the filters) and a tpl_ function draws: tpl_km_simple(adtte_pfs, group = TRT01A) + geom_hline(...), the + on the main plot. New templates: mean_se / mean_ci, waterfall, km_risk_table / km_ci (with ggsurvfit’s add_risktable()) and forest_hr (its own ARD, built by tfl_build_ard(); tpl_forest_hr(ard, ...) and tpl_forest_layout(), the assembly a line of its own). Each figure template declares the statistics its function makes (call_steps); the functions inside tflspec attach no package. The template SPEC, its program and its items written out give the same PNG, and the program written out in full calls no tflspec function.

  • ae_pt_freq and ae_overview draw in a study of the default standard (#402, 0.0.24.9189). A study whose standard folds the row headings (plan_stub(name = "row_label", before = TRUE), as tfl_ai_study_init() writes) stopped on these tables of one row-heading column; rtfreporter 0.8.2.9085 (#701) takes such a column as the stub, and a header cell naming it as the stub. Needs rtfreporter 0.8.2.9085.

  • Template lab_abnormal: subjects with laboratory values in abnormal categories (#400, 0.0.24.9188). n/N (%), a block a parameter, in PARAMN’s order (param_order). The category is an ADaM variable (ANRIND, or criteria levels such as MCRIT1ML), not thresholds; cumulative = TRUE counts a level or worse, baseline_normal = TRUE only subjects normal at baseline. Every parameter analysed keeps its rows, 0/N when no subject is in a category.

  • Template ae_eair: exposure-adjusted incidence rates by SOC and PT (#400, 0.0.24.9188). Each arm’s subjects with the event over their time at risk (to the first event, else the whole exposure, exposure = "TRTDURD"), per per person-years, with cardx::ard_incidence_rate().

  • Template ancova: LS means of the change from baseline and their differences (#400, 0.0.24.9188). Each arm’s LS mean at one visit (cardx::ard_emmeans_emmeans(), the model CHG ~ arm + BASE, covariates) and each other arm’s difference against the reference arm (ref; NULL: the last in the code list, said) with its 95% CI and p-value (cardx::ard_emmeans_contrast(), written by fmt_pvalue()).

  • Template param_change: parameters’ value and change from baseline at each visit (#386, 0.0.24.9187). Laboratory tests, vital signs or ECG parameters (data: ADLB, ADVS, ADEG) – n, mean (SD), median, min, max of AVAL and CHG, a block a parameter (PARAM, its unit in its text) and a visit, in the order of PARAMN and AVISITN. Each arm’s value and change side by side under the arm and its N (layout = "cols"), or the change’s rows under the value’s ("rows"). The change is read from the records that have one, so the baseline visit’s change cells are empty. params, visits and where are all records unless given (where = 'ANL01FL == "Y"' in the examples). Needs rtfreporter 0.8.2.9084 (the arm’s N over its two columns).

  • Template headings given by name merge with the defaults’; a template’s default variables are those the data has (#393, 0.0.24.9186). labels: {RACE: "Race, n (%) [a]"} in a template SPEC changed every other heading to NA (the whole default replaced): now labels and param_labels given by name change those names only, and RACE: ~ drops one (cells are the rows given). An ARD analysis may say optional: true (the analyses sheet’s new column): its variables are written any_of(c(...)), the ones the data has, and tfl_build_ard() says which it left out. demog and disposition set it for the variables a report does not name, so demog runs on an ADSL with no ETHNIC; a report’s own variables are as written (a misspelling stops). ARS export leaves the flag out (tflspec’s own).

  • Template parameters from the study standard (#392, 0.0.24.9185). tfl_param(study = ) also takes "output.population" (the report’s population:) and "settings.treatment" (study.yml’s new settings: treatment:); population, by and group take them by their names, so a report with population: SAF need not write it again. A value comes from the report’s arguments, the study standard, a variant’s defaults, the template’s. tfl_test_templates() lists an analysis set or treatment parameter with no study source. km_simple takes population (the analysis set’s id) in place of the flag pop: its subjects are kept by data.yml’s definition, a semi join of the figure’s data (the join step’s new how = "semi": semi_join(adsl |> filter(SAFFL == "Y") |> select(USUBJID), by = "USUBJID")), whatever the figure’s data has. tfl_fig_template()’s pop stays (the figure designer’s presets).

  • ae_max_grade’s ARD builds in a study (#394, 0.0.24.9184). Its analysis data made by code (each subject’s highest record) had no from, and the ARD definition’s check stopped (“from is blank”); each says the records it is made from now.

  • tfl_template_variant(): a template by its defaults alone (#388, 0.0.24.9183). tfl_template_variant("demog_jp", from = "demog", defaults = list(...)) registers from’s parameters, types and body with other defaults, no R body; it reads from as it is when it runs, so a fix to it reaches the variant. The same name replaces from (with a message). A value comes from the report’s arguments, then the study standard, the variant’s defaults, from’s. A report’s program calls from’s tpl_*() with the variant’s defaults written out, under # template <name>: a variant of <from> (<package> <version>). tfl_templates() has a from column. A study’s spec/templates/*.R is run when the study is read (tfl_read_study_spec()), and tfl_use_company_templates() writes one variant a template, its package exporting nothing.

  • tfl_param(type = ): each template parameter’s input type (#387, 0.0.24.9182). "vars", "levels", "flag", "number", "text", "choice" (with choices) or "list" (with fields), and multiple, in tfl_template_params() – what tflplanner’s template SPEC form reads in place of guessing from the default. Levels say whose values they are (of: by_levels of by, params of PARAMCD). Every tflspec template’s parameters have theirs; a company’s without one takes tflspec’s for its name, else one read from its default, which tfl_test_templates() lists ("no type"). The schema says each plan function’s tier (required, usual, other): which cards tflplanner’s builder shows from the start.

  • Template ae_max_grade: adverse events by SOC and PT at the maximum severity or grade (#385, 0.0.24.9181). Each subject once, at the highest severity (AESEV) or grade (AETOXGR) of their events – overall, in each SOC, in each PT (dplyr::slice_max() in the ARD program). The grades are rows under each term (grade_in = "rows", as FDA’s tables), or columns in each arm with its “Any grade” column first ("cols"). The overall block is first; the SOCs and PTs by their count (sort = "n") or by name ("name"). Needs rtfreporter 0.8.2.9083.

  • Template ae_pt_freq: adverse events by preferred term, most frequent first (#383, 0.0.24.9180), the first of the safety templates. The treatment-emergent events’ preferred terms, the subjects with any event first, then the terms by decreasing frequency in the first group of the code list of by (sort_by names another column). min_pct keeps the terms of that percentage of subjects or more, in any column (as FDA’s tables of common adverse events), in all (min_pct_in = "all") or in the Total column ("total"). tpl_ae_pt_freq() is its call.

  • shift / lab_shift as a template SPEC (#382, 0.0.24.9179). Written as template: in a report file, they stopped with “vars needs at least two columns” in a study whose defaults say plan_stub: {name, before} (as SAMPLE-01’s do): the template’s plan_stub(vars = ) was taken for the look and the study’s replaced it. An item is the look now only when all its arguments are: the stub’s columns stay. Every template’s template: form is now tested against its written-out items.

  • The AI steps over several workbooks (#378, 0.0.24.9178). tfl_ai_read_shell(path, shells = ) reads a TOC in one workbook and its shells in others: each report’s shell is looked for in all of them (a sheet named as one already there is "<sheet> [<workbook>]", its own name kept), the text has a part a workbook, and each report’s place names its workbook. tfl_ai_prepare(toc, shells = , add = TRUE) (and tfl_ai_write_requests(add = TRUE)) adds a workbook’s reports to the study’s requests and answers already there – tables and figures, then listings, then a book of PK figures, one at a time: the new requests are named after those there (ae-2), a report asked for already stops the call (overwrite = TRUE asks for it again), spec/toc.yml gets the new reports at its end. The requests (tfl_ai_requests() too) and tfl_ai_prepare()’s toc have a book column.

  • Figures in the AI steps (#376, 0.0.24.9177). A figure of the TOC is a request of its own (figure-1 …: its shell from the workbook, its analysis set, the ADaM summary, the figure templates); its answer, a figure design, is checked and written as the figure’s report file in the design’s form – the same design back for tflplanner’s figure designer – and tfl_ai_run() draws it as tflplanner does (tfl_fig_design_code()): its PNG and its RTF. The requests and the reports have a type column (table, figure), the run’s reports a png. A figure’s assumptions with their questions join ai/questions.md. tfl_ai_write_requests(types = ) now defaults to tables and figures. New tfl_ai_questions() and tfl_ai_answer_questions() read the questions and write the person’s answers (each into its - Answer:, the rest as it is), and tfl_ai_prepare(mode = "agent") returns agent_prompt, the agent’s first message, also written to ai/agent_prompt.md. The example workbook has a Kaplan-Meier figure, with its stored answer.

  • tfl_ai_prepare(mode = "agent"): the study’s requests for a coding agent (#374, 0.0.24.9176), GitHub Copilot’s agent in VS Code and the like. The agent works through every request without stopping: it saves an answer, runs run.R, reads ai/status.md and repairs. What it cannot settle it takes a guess on and asks as an assumption’s question. The new tfl_ai_run() (what run.R calls) collects the answers, builds each report’s ARD and RTF – one report’s failure not stopping the others – and writes ai/status.md. It also gathers the questions into ai/questions.md: one question asked by several reports once, the reports listed, an answer there kept. The person answers it; the agent moves the answers to ai/decisions.md and redoes the reports they touch. The instructions (AGENTS.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md) tell the agent to work from the ADaM summary and read the ADaM with R only to settle a question the summary does not (with the company’s approved AI; a chat is sent the summary only). Each request gives the shells’ text and where each report’s shell is in the TOC / SHELL workbook file (tfl_ai_write_requests(workbook = "file"): the file, the sheet, the cells, the TOC row); the agent reads that place alone with R when the text looks cut, never another sheet on a guess. For tflplanner: a new study’s RTF files go to output/tfl, its programs to programs/tfl, and tfl_ai_prepare() writes spec/toc.yml (the TOC’s reports in order, with their section and analysis set) when the study has none. The guide’s step 6 is now tfl_ai_run(".").

  • The AI steps return what a screen needs (#371, 0.0.24.9175), for tflplanner’s AI page. tfl_ai_prepare() returns a tfl_ai_prepared list: requests, toc (each report of the TOC, its shell found or not, the request asking for it), sheets, adam (the ADaM summary), files (written, relative to the study) and next_steps. dry_run = TRUE reads the workbook and the ADaM and writes nothing (to look before the requests are written); adam_summary = reuses a call’s $adam. tfl_ai_collect_answers() returns a tfl_ai_collected list: reports (the data frame it returned, with problems_text – every problem –, file and repair), next_steps, assumptions, stray; its print is as before. res$status is now res$reports$status. New tfl_ai_save_answer(study_dir, request, text) writes a pasted answer where the collect reads it (ai/answers/<request>.md, UTF-8), and tfl_ai_requests(study_dir) reads the requests written again. tfl_ai_prepare() also takes datasets and max_levels (the ADaM summary’s) and quiet, and returns the workbook reading’s notes as hint. A request no longer shows where the ADaM is: its copy of spec/data.yml names each dataset’s file alone (path: adsl.xpt), the study’s own file keeping the full path.

  • A line break inside a cell no longer shifts the shells’ text (#370, 0.0.24.9174). tfl_ai_read_shell() missed a cell whose text holds a line break (Alt+Enter in Excel: a column header like “Placebo” over “(N=xx)”), and every later cell of the workbook took the text of the one before it – the shells and the TOC titles the AI read were wrong. The workbook reader now reads such a cell as one (\n in the text), and the cells after it keep their own text.

  • A nested count with no records: the overall row 0, not a stop (#367, 0.0.24.9173). cards::ard_stack_hierarchical() stops on data with no record (“all missing”), so a table of zero events – common in a study – could not be made. The ARD program now calls the study helper ard_hierarchical_or_none() with the same arguments: cards’ ARD with records; with none, the overall row (with over_variables = TRUE) n = 0 and p = 0 with each group’s N, and the groups’ counts. The table is “Any … 0 (0.0)” alone. complete_hierarchy() adds nothing under an overall row of 0 unless when_none = TRUE. ARS still shows cards’ function.

  • An AI answer’s overall row made (#366, 0.0.24.9172). An answer that names an overall row (normalize_ard: {overall: ...}) without over_variables = TRUE on its hierarchical analysis had no such row; tfl_ai_collect_answers() now writes over_variables = TRUE into that analysis in the report file and adds an assumption saying tflspec added it. A spec written by hand keeps the check’s warning.

  • AI requests with the TOC / SHELL workbook attached, and tfl_ai_prepare() (#364, 0.0.24.9171). tfl_ai_write_requests(workbook = ): "text" (default) as before; "attach" – each request says where its reports’ shells are in the attached workbook (sheet, cells, TOC row) instead of their text; "both" – the places and the text, the attachment right where they differ. For a workbook whose text is not read right, when the chat takes an Excel file. tfl_ai_prepare(dir, toc, ...) runs the guide’s step 3 in one call (tfl_ai_study_init() only when there is no study.yml, the ADaM summary, the workbook read, the requests). The AI table guide (English and Japanese) shows both.

  • AI answers as a tester’s chat writes them (#365, 0.0.24.9170). A report number as the TOC writes it (Table 15.3.1.3.13.a, as the prompt asks) is the report file’s id with letters, digits, ., _ and - only (Table-15.3.1.3.13.a), its assumptions too; it could not be read before. tfl_ai_collect_answers() takes an answer’s report named another way (T-15.3.1.3.13.a) as the one whose number it is. The check now says what stopped later: a table with no column key (an error: one arm too, the arm as by and cols) and an overall row no hierarchical analysis makes (a warning: over_variables = TRUE); the table prompt says both. An answer with none of its request’s reports no longer says “done”.

  • An ARD that is not cards’ in the code lists’ order: relevel_ard() (#362, 0.0.24.9169). cardx’s survfit keeps its rows in the arms’ order but makes their factor again, in alphabetical order, so a survfit table’s arms came out alphabetical unless the report said plan_levels(TRT01A = ). The ARD program now writes relevel_ard(TRT01A = cl_trt01a) after an analysis that is not cards’ (custom code, cardx, a study’s own function) reading a column with a code list: the column’s levels in the list’s order, its values and rows as they were (a study helper, tfl_helpers_code()). So #352 leaves out a plan_levels() entry equal to the code list whatever analysis reads it, and the km_table and orr templates write none for the arms (an order given, by_levels, stays). The tables are the same; SAMPLE-01’s T-14-2-2 gives the same RTF without its plan_levels(TRT01A = ). Such a report’s ARD fingerprint changes, so an ARD made before is made again.

  • A nested count’s code-list values counted 0: complete_hierarchy() (#357, 0.0.24.9168). cards’ ard_stack_hierarchical() counts only the values some group has, so a fixed SOC / PT no subject has could not be shown. complete_hierarchy() in an analysis’s post adds them, n = 0 and p = 0 in every group (the Total column too), N the group’s: the outermost variable’s from its code list, an inner one’s where the codelists sheet’s new column under names its parent (a value without one is not added, and the program says so). The rows keep the code lists’ order. The generated code writes it in full (variables = the row’s, under = the lists’, as they are in the ARD); it is one of the study helpers (tfl_helpers_code()). Without it nothing changes, and a study whose code lists have no under keeps its fingerprints.

  • A named order, and the variables’ headings under variable = (#356, 0.0.24.9167; rtfreporter #679, 0.8.2.9075). plan_levels() may name its values’ text, as factor(levels, labels) (plan_levels(SEX = c(F = "Female", M = "Male"))): the schema takes a map (value: text), the sheets’ levels cell F = Female | M = Male, both ways, and a named order is never left out as the ARD’s own. The variables’ headings are written plan_labels(variable = c(AGE = "Age (years)", ...)) (the sheets’ bridge and the templates), so they never meet a variable’s value labels; a report that says plan_labels(AGE = ) reads as before, and a named plan_levels(variable = ) comes back as the headings. The tables are the same.

  • plan_levels() the ARD already says is not written (#352, 0.0.24.9166). A table’s program (tfl_content_code()) and its run (tfl_content_run()) leave out a column’s order that is the report’s code list – applied when the ARD is made, a factor cards keeps in its order – when every analysis reading the column is cards’, and variable = when it is the order of the ARD’s analyses. T-14-1-1’s program loses its plan_levels() and the code lists at its head. The templates of cards’ analyses (demog, summary and those on it, hierarchical, ae_overview; shift’s columns) write none, so their call has no codelists = either. Kept: an order of the report’s own, a column no analysis reads, one a cardx analysis reads (survfit names the arms from the strata: T-14-2-2) and a report whose data steps make its data. A workbook’s table (tfl_table_code(ard_spec = )) leaves out the same, so it and its YAML file write one program. The RTF is the same.

  • The AI table guide’s install lines (#360, 0.0.24.9165). A new R has no remotes, and the sample’s efficacy table needs broom (cardx’s confidence intervals): the guide (English and Japanese) now installs remotes, cards, cardx, haven and broom first, then the two packages from GitHub. It also says that the widen_ard() notes printed while making the RTF are information, and what to do when tfl_build_ard() asks for a package.

  • Fix: the study’s ARD program puts a report’s code lists on its data (#353, 0.0.24.9164). When a report’s analysis data was its population under a name (adsl_saf <- pop_saf), the study’s program wrote the code lists but did not apply them (set_levels() was taken off pop_saf, as a data the analyses do not read), so the ARD kept the raw codes: SAMPLE-01’s T-14-1-1 printed “F” / “M” where its code list says “Female” / “Male”. One report’s program was right. Now each report’s ARD is the same from the study’s program as from its own; the tables show the code lists’ labels, order and 0-count levels.

  • plan_levels() before plan_labels() (#349, 0.0.24.9163): the values’ order first, then their names and the variables’. The schema’s ranks swap (plan_levels 80, plan_labels 90), the cards’ and the generated code’s order, and the templates write them so. The table is the same: rtfreporter applies the two together, whatever their order (checked for the variables’ order and headings, value labels, and a column the plan makes). A file that writes plan_labels() first reads as before.

  • The rounding in either case (#347, 0.0.24.9162; rtfreporter #676). The study sheet’s rounding and a YAML file’s plan_digits: {rounding: } (a report, defaults.yml, a pattern, a style) are read in lower case: “SAS” is “sas”. The generated code writes “sas” / “r” as before, so it needs no newer rtfreporter.

  • Template SPEC: the study’s styles, a template’s look under them, and where titles and footnotes print (#344, 0.0.24.9160).

    • defaults.yml may hold named styles, styles: {compact: {content:, page:}}: the look a report picks with style: compact (none named: standard). The style is the nearest layer below the report’s own; its items are marked style:<name> and the program says # (study style: compact). tfl_write_study_part("defaults") writes them. SAMPLE-01’s patterns/Compact moved to styles: compact gives the same RTF for all its tables.
    • A template’s look (plan_style, plan_blanks, plan_columns, plan_digits, the rows a page …) is under the study’s layers, which say the look and win (decided 10/17); its shape stays over them. The template’s call (A) has the study’s lines after it, and tfl_template_to_spec()
      1. leaves the study’s look to the layers: the same table.
    • study.yml’s settings: titles_at: header | titles and footnotes_at: footer | footnotes (decided 10/17): header puts a report’s titles (page.titles) in the running header after the study’s lines, footer its footnotes in the running footer before them; titles / footnotes, or no setting, keep them above and below the table.

  • Template SPEC: a company’s templates (#343, 0.0.24.9159). A company’s templates are an R package of its own (decided 2026-10-17). tfl_template() registers a template from outside (its kind, layout, parameters, body, the function its program calls and an example); a name already registered is replaced with a message, and a parameter that changes the look (the rows a page, widths, digits, blank rows, the style) is warned about. tfl_param() is exported; tfl_template_params() gives a template’s parameters to start from; tfl_template_run() is the A use of any template, what a company’s exported functions call. tfl_test_templates() runs each template with one parameter at a time changed and lists those that change the look – tflspec’s own have none. tfl_use_company_templates() writes a company’s package to start from: a thin wrapper of each tflspec template chosen (the same parameters, the company’s defaults, tflspec’s body), registered on load, its function, tests, the company’s study defaults and a README; it installs and its tests pass. tfl_templates() gains package and call.

  • Template SPEC in a report’s YAML (#341, 0.0.24.9158). A report’s file may be template: {name, args}, its ard: / data: / content: holding only what it adds or changes (tfl_output(template = ); read and written, a named vector in args as a map; a figure designer’s template: km_simple, a name, is not one). tfl_resolve_output() puts the template’s items between the study’s layers and the report’s own (each marked template:<name>), and its ard: under the report’s; a parameter that says where its study default is (plan_cells.continuous for summary / demog’s cells) takes it, and a SPEC value over a different one says so. The program (tfl_content_code()) is the template’s call, plan <- tpl_x(ard, ...), with the study’s and the report’s own lines after it, each marked (A); template = "items" writes the items instead, as it does when the call cannot say the report’s own table roles, data or normalization. tfl_template_to_spec() writes a template report out as its items (B). The sheets, and so the study’s ARD program, take a template report’s items and analyses. SAMPLE-01’s nine template reports, written as template SPECs, give the same ARD and the same RTF now, by B and by A.

  • AI kit: the first try on a Japanese Windows PC (#338, 0.0.24.9157). tfl_ai_collect_answers() and tfl_ai_unpack() read an answer saved as UTF-8 with or without a BOM, with CRLF line ends, or as UTF-16 (Notepad’s “Unicode”). They also read an answer Notepad saved as <request>.md.txt. An answer saved in Shift-JIS / CP932 is an error that says how to save it again as UTF-8. Every file the kit writes (requests, index, ADaM summary, TOC/shell text, repairs, the study’s YAML, the report files) is UTF-8 whatever the session’s locale, and the folder of file = "ai/..." is made when it is missing. tfl_ai_write_requests() makes ai/answers and says what to paste first. The print of tfl_ai_collect_answers() gives each request’s status, its reports and the next step (paste the repair into the same chat, the request into a new one …). It also names answers whose file name matches no request. An error when writing one request’s reports no longer stops the other requests. tfl_ai_read_shell() on a company’s own workbook: a sheet named like a TOC must list report numbers and must not be named by one (a shell sheet named L-16-2-1 <list> is not taken for the TOC). A header cell saying title (Title, or the Japanese words for it) gives the title column, so a longer analysis-set column is not taken for the title. Full-width digits in a report number are read. The print says what to pass when no TOC or a report’s shell was found (toc_sheet =, sheets =). A request’s own read of the workbook keeps the toc_sheet and sheets given. The table guides’ sample block uses one stored answer per request (inst/ai/example/answers/), so all four reports print ok. The block and the guide’s steps 3 and 6 are run as tests.

  • Where a table’s page names print, said in its content (#337, 0.0.24.9156; rtfreporter #672). plan_paginate_group(heading_at = ) and plan_paginate_rows(heading_at = ) (section, title, none) are in the schema, and the sheets’ layout gains group_heading_at and pages_heading_at, both ways. It is the default of the report’s rtf_tables(auto_section = , auto_title = ): a report’s own setting (the page’s rtf_tables: {auto_section: }, the report sheet’s auto_section) wins, and a blank one does not undo it. Needs rtfreporter 0.8.2.9072.

  • Template SPEC: ae_overview (#335, 0.0.24.9155). A display template on summary (tpl_ae_overview()): the subjects with a treatment-emergent adverse event of each kind – any, related, grade 3 or higher, serious, leading to discontinuation, leading to death – n (%) by arm, a row a kind. Each row is a subjects analysis of the events its where keeps; flags changes the rows. The onco example study gains the report it is checked against (T-14-3-2, Overview of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events); the template gives the same items and RTF by A, by B and by its spec.

  • Template SPEC: four more (#333, 0.0.24.9154). summary takes an optional mean (95% CI) analysis of its continuous variables (ci_label; T-14-2-3). km_table (tpl_km_table()): the Kaplan-Meier median and event-free rates, from the ARD – its survival analyses stay the report’s own, as decided (T-14-2-2). vs_change on summary (tpl_vs_change()): a vital sign’s baseline, value and change at one visit (T-14-2-1). orr (tpl_orr()): the best overall response and the objective response rate with its CI (the AI example’s T-14-2-1). Each gives the same items and RTF by A, by B and by its spec file.

  • Template SPEC: summary takes categorical variables, and disposition (#331, 0.0.24.9153). The layout summary takes categorical beside the continuous variables (either or both), the subjects-per-group and categorical analyses’ labels and the categorical statistics (NULL: cards’ own); a parameter given as NULL is “none”, not the template’s default. The look (the rows a page) is no parameter: a report changes it with an item of its own (T-14-1-3’s plan_paginate_rows(max_rows = 24)). The display template disposition (tpl_disposition()) on it: the status at the end of the study. On the sample study T-14-1-2 (disposition), T-14-1-3 and T-14-1-4 (summary) give the same items and RTF by A, by B and by their spec files, and T-14-2-1 still does. The layout shift (a category at baseline by the same after it, a block a parameter) and the display template lab_shift on it (tpl_shift(), tpl_lab_shift()): the AI example’s T-14-3-5 gives the same items and RTF by both. The layout listing (tpl_listing()): a dataset’s records, their order and the columns – a column’s width is part of its definition, the one look a template takes; the sample study’s L-16-2-7 gives the same data, items and RTF by A and by B.

  • For a builder of the YAML’s items (#329, 0.0.24.9152; tflplanner B3). tfl_resolve_output(provenance = TRUE) says where each item’s arguments come from (arg_from: own, defaults, pattern:<name>, by argument – a verb whose ... is named by top-level key) and gives the item below it (without the report’s own layer: what a revert goes back to); provenance = FALSE is as before. One item: tfl_item_code() (its call), tfl_item_written() (the arguments its code writes), tfl_item_own() (what the report’s own layer holds of it over below). tfl_schema(fn) has the function’s formals (the data’s arguments left out) and the required ones. tfl_write_study_part() writes the study’s defaults, a pattern, its code lists, data or TOC back to its file (the sample study’s files written back are byte-identical).

  • A report file reads and writes back as the same text (#327, 0.0.24.9151). tfl_write_output() writes the list-valued keys of the ard: part (analysis_data add/keep/distinct; analyses by/strata/variables/ statistics/formats) and listing_col vars as a sequence even when they hold one name, as the sheets bridge does; they were written as a scalar.

  • Template SPEC, a first prototype (#325, 0.0.24.9150). A report kind from a few parameters, one definition for two uses: tpl_demog() / tpl_summary() give the table plan (A: the program’s one call, the study’s defaults written after it), tfl_template_expand() the report’s items (B: saved into its YAML, marked template:<name>). The layout template summary (continuous variables by a column key) and the display template demog on it; the layout hierarchical and ae_soc_pt on it (tpl_ae_soc_pt(), tpl_hierarchical()); tfl_templates() lists them. On the sample study T-14-1-1, T-14-1-1S (demog(stack = TRUE)), T-14-2-1 (summary) and T-14-3-1 (ae_soc_pt) give the same RTF by A, by B and by their spec files. km_simple (the figure template) is on the registry too: the sample study’s F-14-2-3, written as the template and its own items after it (a median line, three tfl_ard_number(), the y axis’ title), draws the same PNG as its design-form file. Many reports at once in Excel: tfl_read_template_sheets() reads a workbook of two sheets (templates, template_rows) and tfl_write_template_yaml() writes each report’s file; the example (inst/extdata/template-spec/, DM and AE, the workbook and the same as YAML) gives the sample study’s items exactly.

  • A table whose data steps normalize the ARD: the sheets’ code (#323, 0.0.24.9149). tfl_content_code() and tfl_content_run() no longer write or run the study defaults’ normalize_ard() after a report’s data.steps (the steps make the data; normalizing it again dropped what they did, such as their row labels). With no data steps, normalize_ard() stays first in the one pipe (#303). plan_cells()‘s entries come in the sheets’ order: the table’s variables first, default after.

  • The converter reads a page cell as the sheets do (#321, 0.0.24.9148). tfl_yaml_from_sheets() writes a header, footer, title or footnote cell that is quoted as its text (" Indented": the spaces kept, the quotes not), and a written \n in those cells and in a token’s value as a line break – what the sheets path reads them as. A converted report’s program is the sheets’.

  • The study’s report setup and a report’s tokens from the YAML spec (#317, 0.0.24.9147). tfl_report_setup_code() also takes a study’s spec (tfl_read_study_spec()): its defaults’ page: – the first font of rtf_document: font_table, rtf_default_format: font_size_half_points, tokens, header, footer – written as the sheets saying the same write them, with the names tfl_report_code(output, setup = TRUE, study = ) refers to (study_header, study_header_lines …). tfl_report_tokens() takes a report of the YAML spec and its study. A YAML report’s program (rtf_document(program = )): a study with no settings: program no longer takes its program_dir for it (partial matching), and the report’s id as program_fallback is in the study’s program_dir, as the sheets’ path writes it.

  • Docs: the Pages’ top bar is the package icon’s colour, green #1d5e47 (#313, 0.0.24.9146), as rtfreporter’s bar is its icon’s navy. As rtfreporter’s, the menu puts Reference before Articles, and lists the English articles only: the Japanese one opens from the “In Japanese” toggle at the top of its English page (and back with “In English”).

  • Docs: the AI table-drafting guide says plainly what to try first: one request as it is; when the chat will not take it, the requests again with instructions = "once" (00-instructions.md first in a new chat, then the request) (#318, 0.0.24.9145).

  • A whole study’s AI requests as files (#315, 0.0.24.9142). tfl_ai_write_requests(study_dir, shell, adam, size = ) writes one prompt a request to ai/requests/ – one paste each, no attachment – with an index.md of their reports and lengths; max_chars splits a request too long, instructions = "once" writes the instructions (about 23,000 characters) once to 00-instructions.md. The answers saved as ai/answers/<request>.md are read by tfl_ai_collect_answers(study_dir): each checked against its own request and, with no error, written as report files (only the reports it asked for); one row a report, ok / warning / error / no answer, and the repair prompt of an answer with errors in ai/repairs/.

  • Docs: the AI table-drafting guide (English and Japanese, the article and inst/ai/tflspec-ai-table-guide*.md) rewritten short and practical: what it does, what goes where, what to run, what to give the AI, where its answer goes, and the functions that check it, write the YAML and make the RTF; a whole study with the two functions above; the sample run short.

  • AI drafting of tables’ code spec from a company’s TOC / SHELL workbook (#307, 0.0.24.9141). A new drafting task, table: a batch of 5 to 10 tables becomes report files of the YAML spec (spec/outputs/<id>.yml: ard: analyses, data:, codelists:, content: items, page:) over the study’s defaults. tfl_ai_context("table", outputs, shell, datasets, study_dir, examples), tfl_ai_prompt("table") (the schema from tfl_schema(), tfl_spec_columns() and tfl_ard_methods(); a reviewed report of the family as the model with examples =), tfl_ai_parse() (one YAML block, outputs: read as tfl_read_output() reads a file), tfl_ai_check() (the schema: unknown functions and arguments, types, required arguments; the ARD’s fields and methods; the analysis sets; the datasets and variables of the ADaM summary; the ARD program and the table code written from a copy of the study folder, nothing run) and tfl_ai_unpack() (one file a report; the assumptions join spec/_assumptions.yml, batch by batch). New helpers: tfl_ai_read_shell() (any workbook layout as compact text: every sheet, non-empty cells in reading order, merged cells once, indents; pick reports by number or sheets; a size cap), tfl_ai_adam_summary() (a folder of XPT: variables, labels, types, short value lists, no records), tfl_ai_batches() (the TOC’s tables by family) and tfl_ai_study_init() (study.yml, spec/data.yml with ADSL’s analysis sets, spec/defaults.yml). The AI user manual takes the code spec as its main path (the sheet spec is Appendix A), and a tester guide in English and Japanese ships in inst/ai/ (articles “Drafting tables’ code spec with an AI chat”). A sample TOC / SHELL workbook and a stored answer are in inst/ai/example/.

  • tfl_as_table_spec() takes the variables’ order from plan_levels(variable = ) (#311, 0.0.24.9140), not from the order of plan_labels(): a label sets only the text (rtfreporter #666). A plan’s plan_levels(variable = ) no longer becomes a variables row named variable.

  • The sheets from a spec in memory: tfl_sheets_from_spec(study, outputs) (#304, 0.0.24.9139). What tfl_sheets_from_yaml(dir) does, from a study and its reports already read (tfl_read_study_spec(), tfl_read_outputs()) or changed in memory and not written yet; tfl_sheets_from_yaml(dir) is now tfl_sheets_from_spec() of what it reads, its result unchanged.

  • A test compares a listing’s content code (tfl_content_code()) with the sheets’ tfl_listing_code(): the same pages (RTF) on the data the sheets’ program makes. tfl_content_code() does not write the listing’s data part (dataset, where, sort, dates), and writes a label’s \n as it is where the sheets make it a line break (a skipped test until it does).

  • tfl_args_from_r() keeps a NULL argument on R < 4.4 (#305, 0.0.24.9138). label = NULL read as no argument on R 4.2 (is.atomic(NULL) is TRUE there); it is tfl_r("NULL") on every R now.

  • The table’s code is one pipe from the ARD (#302, 0.0.24.9137). tfl_table_code() writes plan <- ard |> normalize_ard(...) |> table_plan(...) |> plan_*(): normalize_ard()’s hierarchy, overall and stack are the ones tfl_normalize_code() writes (new ard_spec; with no ARD definition, the hierarchy the rows and label say, as the spec files take it). data is now the ARD’s name ("ard"); normalize = FALSE writes plan <- table_plan(data, ...) as before, for a program that normalizes the ARD itself.

  • plan_levels()‘s names come in one order, whatever the sheets’ rows: variable, the column keys, the row and stack keys, then the categorical variables.

  • The digits sheet takes significant digits: 3s is {mean:.3s}.

  • The variables’ order is plan_levels(variable = ) (#300, 0.0.24.9136). The variables sheet’s order is written as plan_levels(variable = c("AGE", "SEX", ...)) (the values of the ARD’s variable column; a variable nested with under has its place from plan_nest()), and read back from it. It used to reach the table only through the order of the names in plan_labels(), and a variable with an order but no label was not ordered. plan_labels() sets no order now and comes back in the order it was written: SAMPLE-01’s tables are byte-identical, from the YAML and through the sheets. The sheets read back from content keep the variables’ rows in their place: plan_levels() is read before plan_labels() wherever it is written (the recommended order of #290 puts the labels first, which moved a variable with levels but no label, e.g. TRT01A, to the end – and its code list with it in tflplanner’s programs).

  • The onco sample study: screen failures, ethnicity, study disposition, an AE time-to-event endpoint (#298, 0.0.24.9135). adsl holds every screened subject: the 160 randomised and 40 screen failures, who have no arm (ARM, TRT01P … NA, ARMNRS “SCREEN FAILURE”, as SDTMIG 3.3 has it; the factors keep their two levels) and no records in the other datasets. New ADSL variables: ETHNIC, RFICDT (informed consent), ENRLFL (enrolled: randomised), ARMNRS, and the study disposition EOSSTT, EOSDT, DCSREAS, DCSREASP (a randomised subject is in follow-up until death; a screen failure ends at screening). adtte has a safety endpoint, TTSKIN: the time to the first treatment-emergent skin and subcutaneous tissue disorder of the safety set, in days from the first dose, censored at the end of the treatment-emergent period. The new values are drawn after the old ones (same seed): every existing record keeps its values, and the other six datasets are unchanged. An analysis of the randomised subjects selects them (ITTFL, SAFFL, EFFFL): adsl now has 200 rows. The SAP and CRF outline in system.file("sample", "onco", package = "tflspec") say the same.

  • The samples run on the oncology sample study (#295, 0.0.24.9134). tflspec’s examples, articles, README and AI kit use adsl, adae, adrs … (study XYZ-ONC-01, Drug X vs Control) instead of the CDISC pilot data (cards::ADSL, pharmaverseadam), which is dropped from Suggests. inst/examples/onco/ replaces inst/examples/pharmaverseadam/: a study folder whose specs (ARD spec, table and report specs, plot list) are written into programs and run – demographics, best overall response with ORR and DCR, TEAEs by SOC and PT, PFS and OS Kaplan-Meier plots, a PFS forest plot, waterfall, swimmer and spider plots. The example workbooks of inst/extdata/ard-spec (made by data-raw/ard-spec-examples/make-examples.R) are built from the sample study: the response rate from its best overall response, the laboratory shift from its CTCAE grades. inst/extdata/spec-yaml and the define’s code lists use its arms and age groups. The AI kit’s made-up study XYZ-001 reads the same data. The datasets’ help pages link to each other (they linked to pharmaverseadam’s and ggsurvfit’s topics of the same names). No function changes.

  • A value’s labels in the report’s code list (#294, 0.0.24.9133; the user’s decision of 2026-10-16). The key columns a plan makes itself – a stack’s pair (tables$stack: subgroup, subgroup_level) and the groups of statistics (.stat_group) – are not in the data, so the ARD program cannot put a code list on them: the bridge writes their code list rows as plan_labels(subgroup = c(ALL = "All Subjects")) and reads that call back as code list rows (tfl_sheets_from_yaml() passes it the report’s normalize_ard()). Their order stays the plan’s (no plan_levels() from the list, so a list naming some values drops none). A data variable’s value labels stay its code list’s, which the ARD program puts on the data; plan_labels() of one is listed in not_converted with where they go. tfl_args_from_r() reads plan_labels(c(AGE = "Age")) and plan_levels() given one named vector, as rtfreporter does (the schema’s map: true).

  • An oncology sample study: adsl, adex, adae, adlb, advs, adrs, adtr, adtte (#291, 0.0.24.9132). Simulated ADaM datasets of study XYZ-ONC-01 (Drug X vs Control, 1:1, RECIST 1.1 every 6 weeks, cut-off 30 June 2026; 160 subjects; not real patient data), with CDISC names and labels; TRT01P, TRT01A and ARM are factors with Drug X first. They agree with one another, being made from one set of simulated subject histories: a confirmed CR/PR has its tumour sizes 30% (CR: 0 mm) below baseline, nothing is assessed after progression, the PFS and OS events are the progressions and the deaths (DTHFL, DTHDT), doses stop at progression, toxicity, death or the cut-off, and a reduced dose follows a grade >= 3 adverse event. The recipe is data-raw/gen_onco.R (seeded, base R); the study’s mini SAP (populations, endpoints, a display list) and CRF outline are installed in system.file("sample", "onco", package = "tflspec"). LazyData: true.

  • tfl_args_from_r() round trips (#288, 0.0.24.9131; found by S2): an argument the schema takes as an integer comes back an integer (26, not 26.0), and a figure function’s arguments keep the order they were written in (the positional ones named in their places).

  • The plan verbs in one recommended order (#289, 0.0.24.9130; the user’s decision of 2026-10-16): the order a person designs a table in – normalize_ard, then the mapping (table_plan, plan_cells, plan_stat_groups, plan_total, plan_compare, plan_filter), then the finishing (plan_labels, plan_levels, plan_nest, plan_digits, plan_sort, plan_col_header, plan_stub, plan_blanks, the pages, plan_row_group, plan_hide, plan_columns, plan_style, plan_cell_style). The schema’s rank follows it, and every plan verb and figure function says its stage (mapping, finishing, or a figure’s output: tfl_schema(fn)$stage); the code a table workbook stands for (tfl_table_code(), tfl_content_code(), the converter) writes its verbs in that order. The tables are the same: SAMPLE-01’s 12 tables give the same RTF byte for byte, and every table case through its workbook and its code the same RTF as its plan.

  • Every design converts; four extension packages in the figure catalog (#286, 0.0.24.9128). tfl_fig_content_from_design() converts a figure type of its own (ae_dot, butterfly, edish, sankey, sunburst, forest_or) to its R (content: !r), which tfl_content_run() runs with the datasets by their names after the figure setup – the same figure; and a composed design (plots: + compose:) to named plots sharing one data part (each plot’s objects renamed after it, df_km, fit_km), compose.layout to wrap_plots() (one row or one column), compose.add to items (& kept as the item’s op), plot.dpi to tfl_image. The figure catalog adds ggrepel’s geom_label_repel, ggtext’s geom_richtext, element_markdown, element_textbox_simple, ggnewscale’s new_scale_fill and ggh4x’s facet_nested, facet_nested_wrap, facetted_pos_scales (in Suggests); a function of a package the program does not attach is written pkg::fn.

  • tfl_fig_template(form = "items") (#284, 0.0.24.9127): a template as a figure report’s content of function calls – template, args (what it was given), data (the report’s data:), content (each item, a named plot’s too, from = "template:<name>", the builder’s mark) and, for a template of its own ARD (forest_hr), analyses. The designer’s design stays the default.

  • tfl_image: a figure drawn at its size on the page (#282, 0.0.24.9126). A figure of items’ tfl_image gives its size on the page (width_in / height_in: inches, or fit, the page’s body) and its resolution (dpi, 300 when not said): the report draws the figure at that size and resolution – rtf_figures(doc, rtfplot(content, render_width =, render_height =, render_dpi =)) – where it drew it at 6.5 x 4.5 in and scaled it into its box (a box of another shape stretched it). With file ({output_id} filled) the figure’s code also saves the image (ggsave(), the same size, in format). A figure of the designer’s pieces is placed as before.

  • A figure’s content as function calls, plot by plot (#280, 0.0.24.9125; the figure designer’s redesign, stage F1). A figure report’s content: is its plot’s items, one a call: the function that makes the plot first (ggplot, ggsurvfit, ggcuminc, or tflspec’s own tfl_risk_panel, tfl_text_column, tfl_n_panel), then its layers (geom_*, annotate, ggsurvfit’s add_*, tfl_ard_number) and its settings (scale_*, coord_*, facet_*, labs, theme_tfl / theme, guides); several plots are named (- km: [items], tfl_plot()) and arranged by patchwork’s items (wrap_plots, plot_layout, plot_annotation); tfl_image is the last item. tfl_content_code() writes it (p_<name> a plot, content <- wrap_plots(...), a position_dodge() said twice as pd) and tfl_content_run() runs it, after the study’s figure setup. The schema has a figure catalog (61 functions: figure:, rank, label in English and Japanese, visible, aes; a catalog geom takes its parameters from the installed layer). tfl_fig_content_from_design() converts a designer’s design once – the 28 templates of ggplot2 and tflplanner’s two designed sample figures draw the same figure (layer data, labels, axis ranges); the 10 figure types of their own become R. tfl_yaml_from_sheets() / tfl_convert_sheets_to_yaml() gain figures = c("design", "items") (the designer’s form stays the default until the designer works in items). tfl_args_to_r() / tfl_args_from_r() write an item’s arguments as R text and read them back (the builder’s R form). The AI kit’s blank and example figure, the manual’s §10.1 and the guide’s figure section are in the new form.

  • A table’s font size is its plan’s (#279, 0.0.24.9124; a user’s PK table warned rtf_tables(font_size_half_points = ) is deprecated). The report sheet’s table_font_size_half_points is the table’s plan_style(font_size_half_points = ) (the sheets’ table code, the converter’s content via the style sheet), no longer rtf_tables()’s (a listing’s pages, made apart by the sheets, still pass it there). A YAML written before, with page: rtf_tables: font_size_half_points, has it moved to the content’s plan_style() by tfl_resolve_output() (the report’s own plan_style key wins): the table keeps its size.

  • An AE table with no ARD definition gets its hierarchy (#278, 0.0.24.9124; a user’s AE table stopped at table_plan(label = ): no column 'AEDECOD'). The sheets knew a table’s hierarchy only from the ARD definition’s hierarchical analysis; a study whose ARD is made by its own program has none. For a report with no ARD definition, the converter takes normalize_ard()’s hierarchy from the table’s rows and label (group1 = AEBODSYS, label = AEDECOD: hierarchy = c("AEBODSYS", "AEDECOD")), its overall from overall_label, and lists it in _not_converted.yml to check. A cell’s line breaks (Excel keeps them as CRLF) are LF in the YAML.

  • An NA argument stays NA; a default template and a report’s rows by name are both kept (#276, 0.0.24.9124; a user’s study converted from the workbooks stopped at table_plan(label = ): no column 'NA'). A logical NA (table_plan(label = NA)) is written .na and read back NA, not the text “NA”. The layering of a named-dots verb keeps a key that is one template in the defaults and rows by name in the report (or the other way) as both, the template first: plan_cells(default = list("{n} ({p}%)", n = ..., orr_ci = ...)), as the sheets make it.

  • A figure with no design gets nothing of a table’s (#274, 0.0.24.9124). The converter gave a figure with no design (and no code of its own), and a listing with no rows, a table’s data and content (table_plan: {}): its data is its own code now (source: code), a listing’s a dataset.

  • A nested variable keeps its place in the round trip (#273, 0.0.24.9123; found by S2 with tflplanner’s SAMPLE-01). A variable under another’s level (under, plan_nest()) with no heading of its own is not in plan_labels(), whose order is the variables’ order: read back from the content (a YAML report to the sheets), it now goes right after the variable it is under, so the variables keep the order they were written in.

  • The converter keeps what tflplanner’s study has (#270, 0.0.24.9122; for tflplanner reading and writing the YAML spec). The listing / figure workbook’s figures sheet (the datasets a figure or report written by hand reads, and whether it reads its ARD) is the report’s data.datasets / data.ard; a row’s note stays (note:), a table’s note is its report’s; R text keeps \n line ends. The sheets back (tfl_sheets_from_yaml()) give them, a blank field as a blank cell (not "NA"), and no figure design for a figure that is its own code.

  • A report’s document says its RTF file (#268, 0.0.24.9121; rtfreporter’s rtf_document(file = ), >= 0.8.2.9063). tfl_report() and tfl_report_code() give the document the path tfl_report_path() says (a YAML report’s with its study), so generate_rtfreport(doc) writes it and the program says its output once, beside its program. A path given to generate_rtfreport() still wins.

  • tfl_report_path() takes a YAML report (#264, 0.0.24.9120). With study = (as tfl_report()): its TOC entry’s file, else study.yml’s settings: file ("{output_id}.rtf" when neither says it), in settings: output_path.

  • The AI kit asks for the study’s YAML files, in one answer (#265, 0.0.24.9119). tflspec_ai_manual(dir) writes seven files (eight with the ADaM metadata, now 07_adam_metadata.csv): the request, the manual, the guide, the schema (03_spec_schema.yml, the installed inst/spec/schema.yml), every file of a study blank (04_blank_spec.md), the example TOC and shells and the answer written from them (06_example_spec.md, made through tfl_yaml_from_sheets()). The chat answers with one Markdown text, a ### <path> heading and a yaml block a file; the new tfl_ai_unpack(answer, dir) writes it into a study folder (only study.yml and spec/**.yml; nothing is written when a path, a duplicate or a block is wrong). tfl_ai_review(dir) reviews a study folder: each report file against the schema (K16-K18), the definition through the workbook’s checks with each finding named by its file and key, spec/_assumptions.yml (K08, K09), the figures; the two prompts go into the folder. A workbook or one report file is reviewed as before. tflspec_ai_manual() loses split (there are no blank workbooks). The manual gains §5, the study folder; the guide is rewritten for the YAML files.

  • The defaults’ content is a table’s (#263, 0.0.24.9117; found by the AI kit). tfl_resolve_output() layers defaults.yml‘s content (normalize_ard, the digits …) onto a table only: a figure or a listing takes the defaults’ page and code lists, not those layers (a figure’s code stopped at “Unknown layer: normalize_ard”).

  • A report’s ARD analyses are its ard: section (#261, 0.0.24.9116; the user’s decision of 2026-10-15: the ARD is made in a stage of its own, before the reports, and every report has the same three steps – 1 data, 2 content, 3 page and output). A report file’s data.analysis_data / data.analyses move to ard: {analysis_data, analyses} (in the report’s own file), and data: keeps what the report reads (source: ard | code | dataset). tfl_output(ard = ); the reader, the writer, the converter, tfl_sheets_from_yaml(), the flat xlsx and its import follow. The generated code is unchanged.

  • The YAML spec, stage 0 (0.0.24.9112; the user’s decision of 2026-10-14 to make YAML the source of a study’s definition, one file a report): the R objects tfl_r() (the !r tag), tfl_unset() (the !unset tag), tfl_call() (a nested {fn:, args:} call), tfl_item() (one layer of content:, a function and its arguments by name) and tfl_output() (one report), with tfl_read_output() / tfl_write_output() for spec/outputs/<id>.yml and the fixtures inst/extdata/spec-yaml/.
